bull.t: Strong revenue growth and AI/HPC demand
bull.b: Revenue momentum provides meaningful operating visibility: Q2 revenue rose 36% year over year, while management expects 2026 growth slightly above 40%. Sustained AI/HPC demand should support utilization, customer engagement, and continued expansion of the foundry franchise.

bull.t: Leading-edge process leadership and high margins
bull.b: The dominant contribution from advanced nodes demonstrates strong process adoption and manufacturing scale. Combined with a 67.7% gross margin, this mix supports durable earnings power and reinforces TSMC’s position as a preferred supplier for complex, performance-sensitive chips.

Substantial liquidity and strong operating cash generation give TSMC flexibility to fund advanced fabs, packaging capacity, dividends, and overseas expansion internally. This financial strength reduces reliance on external financing and helps preserve strategic options through semiconductor cycles.

bear.t: Margin dilution from N2 and overseas fab ramps
bear.b: The next phase of technology and geographic expansion will temporarily pressure profitability as new fabs and nodes ramp below mature-scale economics. Even with strong demand, the projected dilution can moderate margin expansion and make earnings more sensitive to execution and utilization.

bear.t: Advanced packaging capacity is a growth constraint
bear.b: Packaging capacity is an important part of delivering advanced semiconductor systems, so a bottleneck can limit how quickly wafer demand converts into customer shipments and revenue. Planned investment should help over time, but tight capacity remains an execution constraint in the interim.

bear.t: Heavy investment is reducing free-cash-flow conversion
bear.b: TSMC’s ambitious capacity build-out is absorbing a substantial portion of earnings, reducing the amount of profit converted into free cash flow. Continued capital intensity and working-capital requirements could constrain discretionary cash generation even while operating performance remains strong.
